event: Aldous takes the questions straight, one at a time, as a man does who keeps a roll.

changes.note: She owns she doesn't know how she came, an open answer that eases one
Respect, fairness in paying his traded question, and honesty: four more

event: "Sulon. I told you that one. Osric is the king. Osric, second of the name, of House Sable."

memory.fact: Sulon's king is Osric, second of that name, of House Sable.
Sulon's king is Osric, second of that name, of House Sable.

event: "He's a name on the coin and on the tallies to me. Nobody here has seen his face."

memory.fact: To heartland folk the king is a name on coin and tally rather than a face.
To heartland folk the king is a name on coin and tally rather than a face.

event: "Lord Kell holds the vale. The king's steward for the north sits at Aldermere."

memory.fact: The king's steward for the north sits at Aldermere, and the vale's business goes there.
The king's steward for the north sits at Aldermere, and the vale's business goes there.

event: "I answer up through the lord and the steward. Never to the king himself. That's not my place."

memory.fact: A reeve like Aldous answers up through his lord and the king's steward, never to the king.
A reeve like Aldous answers up through his lord and the king's steward, never to the king.

event: Nala asks what's said of magic and monsters, out in the world at large.
He leans on the doorpost. It's an odd thing to be asked, and he weighs it before he answers.
"Every child here knows about mana. Cores. Skills. It's common talk, like the weather."

memory.fact: Every child in the Central Plains knows about mana, core and skills; it is common talk.
Every child in the Central Plains knows about mana, core and skills; it is common talk.

event: "You wake at fourteen and find out what you can do. Some heft a cart. Some heal a cut."
"I've little to speak of and I'm glad of it. Tobin the hunter's the only one here with more."
"Monsters are past the walls. The walls ring the plains, and nobody goes through them."
"Rifts open now and then. When one opens, soldiers come and the village empties out."

memory.fact: Rifts seldom open in the heartland; when one does, soldiers and guild come and villages empty.
Rifts seldom open in the heartland; when one does, soldiers and guild come and villages empty.

event: "I've never seen either one. Most of us die that way, and count it a good life."

memory.fact: Most heartland folk live and die without seeing a monster or a rift.
Most heartland folk live and die without seeing a monster or a rift.

event: He looks at her a while. "Being brought here by magic. That's no tale I've heard in Sulon."
"That's a thing for past the walls, or for a fever. I've no third answer for you."

memory.fact: To Aldous, a stranger brought here by magic is a thing for past the walls, or a fever.
To Aldous, a stranger brought here by magic is a thing for past the walls, or a fever.

event: Bess fills the doorway with a bowl in her hands. "Aldous Crane, she's barefoot in the cold."
She holds the bowl out to Nala. "Mutton. Eat it off my step if you won't come in the house."

memory.fact: Bess will not turn a barefoot woman away hungry, whatever Aldous thinks of her.
Bess will not turn a barefoot woman away hungry, whatever Aldous thinks of her.

event: Aldous says nothing either way about the bowl; he watches Nala's face over it.
"There's no bed for you here. I've a boy in this house and I don't know you."

memory.fact: Aldous will not sleep an unknown stranger under his own roof, with his boy in the house.
Aldous will not sleep an unknown stranger under his own roof, with his boy in the house.

event: "You'll sleep in the Sheaf's loft. Martha takes my word, and my word is you're here till morning."

memory.fact: Aldous lodges strangers in the Sheaf's loft on his word, and Martha takes the reeve's word.
Aldous lodges strangers in the Sheaf's loft on his word, and Martha takes the reeve's word.

event: He walks her across the green; the Sheaf's windows are yellow and the room inside is loud.
Inside is one long smoky room: trestles, a hearth at the far end, a dozen faces turning.

memory.fact: The Sheaf is one long smoky room of trestles and benches, a hearth at the far end.
The Sheaf is one long smoky room of trestles and benches, a hearth at the far end.
Of an evening a dozen or so Harrow men and women drink in the Sheaf after the dusk bell.
Of an evening a dozen or so Harrow men and women drink in the Sheaf after the dusk bell.

event: Martha Deane comes up from the stewpot with a ladle and looks Nala over, head to foot.

memory.fact: Martha Deane, a brisk widow, keeps the Sheaf, Harrow's alehouse on the green.
Martha Deane, a brisk widow, keeps the Sheaf, Harrow's alehouse on the green.

event: "Aldous Crane, what have you brought me?" "A stranger with no token. She answers for it tomorrow."
Martha sets a bowl of mutton and a hunk of dark bread on the nearest trestle in front of her.

memory.fact: The Sheaf serves stew, dark bread and small beer, and has a straw-pallet loft above.

event: The room goes quiet enough to hear the fire, and every face at the trestles turns.
"The fiddler's dead and the Sheaf's had nothing since. You say you can sing. Sing, then."

memory.fact: The Sheaf supper wants a singer; the fiddler who played it last year died in the spring.
